_note: Anti-regrowth surface budget. See THESIS.md, section 'The anti-regrowth brake'. Each ceiling is the exact live count of a governed surface at v5.0.0. The gate (scripts/check-surface-budget.mjs, npm run surface:check) fails the build when any live count exceeds its ceiling. Raising a ceiling requires amending THESIS.md (anti-regrowth section) AND this file in the same commit with a written reason. Sprawl is a deliberate, recorded act, not a drift.

cliCommands.reason: 2026-08-11: +1 (backfill) — the hook has always written ungoverned actions to ~/.dashclaw/orphan-actions.jsonl and told the operator they were 'logged for backfill on guard recovery', but nothing in the repo ever read that file. `dashclaw backfill` is the reader that makes the promise true; without it the audit gap the hook claims to close stays open forever. 2026-07-27: +1 (contained) — Containment Verdicts (governed-autonomy RFC 2026-07-06, feature 3): `dashclaw contained list|diff|apply`, the terminal client for the promote/discard-to-merge lifecycle.

guardPolicyTypes.reason: 2026-09-08: 18 -> 19 catastrophe_floor — the backstop for when the calibrated controller cannot interrupt. A minimum-risk gate on declared destructive action types (default min_risk 85, irreversible-only unless the operator opts out) that fires require_approval (or block) regardless of calibrated theta, and is ungrantable-marked so no allow_grant can disarm it. Staged inactive; activation is operator choice with a guard check. No new routes, tables, migrations, pages, MCP tools, or SDK methods. (Prior: 2026-09-05: 17 -> 18 assumption_hold — converts the advisory assumption alert into authority. Invalidating an assumption already notified the agent (assumption_alerts rides on the guard response) but the verdict stayed allow: permission was still valid while current authority was not, and the agent read the notice and kept going. This type holds the next action above a risk floor by that agent family until a human confirms; hold-not-block by default (escalate_action is require_approval unless the operator opts into block), and relief is the normal path — it runs inside runLocalPolicies, so an approval, a shape grant, or the window elapsing all clear it. No new routes, tables, migrations, pages, MCP tools, or SDK methods; it reads the existing assumptions table through a new repository function. Default packs gain it only under night-shift (window 120) and evidence-first (window 60); every other pack and every existing install is unchanged. (Prior: 2026-08-13: 16 -> 17 deviation_response — per-kind consequence for plan-vs-actual deviation (RFC docs/rfcs/2026-08-11-plan-deviation-events.md). Detection/recording are unconditional and policy-free (a fresh install changes behavior not at all; no default row); this type only maps kind -> warn/require_approval/block, tighten-only, with escalate_action as an explicit ceiling so block is operator opt-in. Rejected the zero-budget risk-folding alternative: it collapses qualitatively different kinds into one dial. No new routes, pages, MCP tools, or SDK methods; one unbudgeted table (plan_deviations). Prior: 2026-08-10 15 -> 16 role_constraint.))
